annotation.summary_en: Conference paper (CLAWAR 2016) addressing ethical concerns arising from Auto-Catastrophic Theory's suggestions on how humanity might survive via and from robots, including cyborgs. Only the abstract is available. It frames living systems as subject to self-destructive and self-preserving processes.
key_provisions_or_claims: Auto-Catastrophic Theory holds 'alive' systems are both auto-catastrophic and auto-survival via protogenic and deuterogenic procedures.
Humans are exposed to autocatastrophes such as natural death and murder.
Raises ethical concerns about humanity surviving via and from robots and cyborgs.
Full text unavailable; only the abstract is available.
annotation.title_clean: Ethical Concerns Of Surviving Via And From Robots: Cyborgs And Expiry Dates
annotation.title_en: Ethical Concerns Of Surviving Via And From Robots: Cyborgs And Expiry Dates
annotation.venue: 19th International Conference on Climbing and Walking Robots and the Support Technologies for Mobile Machines (CLAWAR 2016)
